validity.recommendation: correct or blank StartYear1 (1996 is not supported and is contradicted by independent evidence the system predates it by decades)
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=1996 does not survive scrutiny. Independent, dated evidence places the East Tennessee Natural Gas (ETNG) system's origin far earlier than 1996: (1) Rice University's ArchivesSpace catalog holds records titled 'East Tennessee Natural Gas Company; 1951-1959' (archives.library.rice.edu/repositories/2/archival_objects/57826), i.e. the company was operating and generating records in the early 1950s; (2) Natural Gas Intelligence, 'East Tennessee, Transco Natural Gas Pipes Approved by FERC' (naturalgasintel.com, 2024-03-26), reporting FERC's summary of the System Alignment docket, states ETNG has 'legacy shippers that have steadily received gas since the 1950s'; (3) FERC Federal Register notices from 1996 itself (govinfo.gov FR-1996-07-26/96-19022 and FR-1996-08-27/96-21752) show East Tennessee Natural Gas Company already operating in 1996 under a pre-existing 'blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP82-412-000' -- i.e. it held FERC certification since at least 1982, fourteen years before the sheet's start year; (4) FTC's 1999 clearance of the El Paso-Sonat merger required El Paso to divest ETNG (a Sonat subsidiary) as an established pipeline system 'serving customers in eastern Tennessee and northern Georgia,' completed to Duke Energy Gas Transmission in January 2000 for $386.3 million -- again describing a mature, already-built system, not one about to enter service. None of these sources state a single crisp founding/in-service year, so I am not fabricating a replacement value, but 1996 is affirmatively wrong -- it most likely reflects El Paso's 1996 acquisition of Tenneco (a different, though related, pipeline family) being miscoded onto this row, or a legacy GEM data-entry artifact. Recommend blanking StartYear1 pending a firmer date, or replacing with a pre-1982 placeholder once one is sourced. This is the Start [ref] unit's UNRESOLVED disposition below.

validity.recommendation: no structural change; retain as the sole GEM row for the legacy ETNG mainline
validity.researcher_notes: Existence, classification, ownership and attribution all confirmed independently. ETNG is a real, FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural-gas transmission pipeline (NGA Section 7 certificate holder since at least 1982, Docket CP82-412-000), currently a wholly owned Enbridge subsidiary operating under the legal name 'East Tennessee Natural Gas, LLC' -- confirmed by Natural Gas Intelligence (2024-03-26, naming 'Enbridge Inc.'s East Tennessee Natural Gas LLC (ETNG)') and by Rextag Corporation's independent pipeline-data page (rextag.com/pages/east-tennessee-natural-gas, listing operator 'East Tennessee Natural Gas Company,' owner 'Enbridge, Inc.'). No duplicate: the roster's other 44 rows are unrelated systems; ETNG's two active FERC expansion projects (Ridgeline Expansion Project and System Alignment Project) are already recorded as separate GEM ProjectIDs P5627 and P7809 respectively (confirmed via the live GGIT snapshot) -- neither is in this batch's 45-row roster, so no cross-row lead is filed, but flagging so the orchestrator knows they are not missing/duplicated. Caveat 1 (row type): P0179 'Main Line' functions as a SYSTEM row for the whole ~1,526-mile legacy mainline (like P3221 Carolina Gas Transmission and P0186 KPC elsewhere in this batch) rather than a discrete constructed segment -- this is why Diameter, FuelSource, Pressure, ProposalYear/Month, ConstructionYear/Month and SegmentCost cannot be sourced to single values (see each unit's UNRESOLVED note) and should stay blank rather than be forced. Caveat 2 (geometry orientation): the batch brief flagged that the row's StartState/Province='Tennessee' disagrees with the route geometry, which starts in North Carolina. Every independent source checked (Enbridge's own infopost, Rextag, and GEM's own wiki text) affirms the pipeline runs FROM Tennessee TO Roanoke, Virginia -- so the sheet's Location cells are correct and the route geometry is the reversed/orientation artifact, not the state cells; no attribution concern filed. Caveat 3 (length, immaterial): Wikipedia's 'East Tennessee Natural Gas Pipeline' article states 1,510 mi (2,430 km) versus the sheet's 2,456 km (1,526 mi per two independent current sources, Enbridge infopost and Rextag) -- a ~1% difference. Wikipedia's own reference for this figure is SourceWatch, a sister/predecessor wiki to GEM's own wiki with likely-shared lineage, so I did not treat it as an independent corroborating source and did not use it as a ref; noting the discrepancy here for the record only, not as a spec concern, since two independent, current, non-GEM-lineage sources agree exactly with the sheet's value.

This is a legacy mainline that predates modern FERC e-library dockets and predates GEM's typical proposal-year sourcing window -- no source states when the original East Tennessee system was first proposed. Same gap as ProposalYear/Month: sources place the system in operation 'since the 1950s' (Natural Gas Intelligence, 2024-03-26, quoting FERC's summary of 'legacy shippers') and existing under FERC certification by at least 1982, but no source gives a specific original construction year/month for the mainline as built. No source supports 1996 as the mainline's start/in-service year -- I could not find a source that states it, and multiple independent sources affirmatively contradict it (see the spec concern filed in validity[]: Rice University archival records of the company from 1951-1959; Natural Gas Intelligence 2024-03-26 quoting FERC that ETNG has shippers receiving gas 'since the 1950s'; FERC's own 1996 Federal Register notices showing the company already operating under a 1982 blanket certificate). This is UNRESOLVED as a confirmation of the recorded value (it is not confirmed and should not be treated as sourced), while the disputing evidence is filed as a spec concern with contested={"StartYear1":""} since no source gives a crisp replacement year.

fills.researcher_notes: 2,456 km = 1,526 mi confirmed exactly by two independent, current sources. Note for the record: Wikipedia's article states 1,510 mi (2,430 km), about 1% lower, but its cited source is SourceWatch (a wiki with likely-shared lineage to GEM's own wiki), so I treated it as non-independent and did not cite it or treat the ~1% gap as material against two clean, current, non-GEM-lineage matches.

P0179 'Main Line' is a system-level row covering the whole ~1,526-mile legacy mainline (see validity caveat), not a single constructed segment, and pipe diameter varies along it: FERC/press material on the newer System Alignment project alone describes both a 24-inch pipe next to an existing 16-inch pipe in Tennessee AND an 8-inch-to-24-inch replacement in Virginia on this same system (naturalgasintel.com, 2024-03-26). No single diameter value is truthful for the row as scoped; leaving blank, consistent with how other system rows in this batch (e.g. P3221 Carolina Gas Transmission) are treated.

FuelSource requires a single named upstream field/plant/facility, not a region or commodity (per docs/reference/gem_schema.md). As a system-level mainline, ETNG draws gas from numerous named interconnects (Texas Eastern Transmission, Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Columbia Gulf Transmission, Southern Natural Gas, Midwestern Gas Transmission -- per Enbridge's infopost) plus direct Appalachian-Basin producer connections via its Nora and Jewell Ridge laterals, with Natural Gas Intelligence (2024-03-26) noting a recent shift toward gas 'sourced from the Marcellus and Utica Shales.' No single named field or facility is 'the' source for the whole system, so I left this blank rather than picking one arbitrarily; naming the leads here (Nora, Jewell Ridge, Marcellus/Utica) for whoever revisits this at the segment level.
